newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman's camp denies Croatia election was unfair.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman's camp denies Croatia election was unfair.

text.p: Croatian president Franjo Tudjman's ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) on Tuesday dismissed charges by international monitors that his election victory on Sunday was free but not fair.
"The election was fair and honest," Ivic Pasalic, the head of Tudjman's electoral team, told reporters at the Zagreb headquarters of the HDZ.
A report compiled by observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Monday the presidential election did not meet democratic standards.

"Croatia has experienced a free but not fair election," said U.S. senator Paul Simon, coordinating the monitoring mission organised by the OSCE. "While candidates were able to speak freely, the process leading up to the election was fundamentally flawed."
The pre-election process "did not meet the minimum standards for democracies. By contrast the election itself was, with some exceptions, conducted efficiently," Simon said in a written statement.

Pasalic said Simon's report was not based on facts but on information fed to him by "those (in Croatia) who have been trying for months and years to secure the victory of others and the removal of Tudjman and the HDZ".
"As far as I know, when he arrived, the chief of the OSCE mission did not know who the presidential candidates were, and it took him 10 minutes to find Croatia on the map of the world," Pasalic said.
Pasalic also dismissed the main objection of the report -- that the state media, especially national television, favoured Tudjman at the expense of the two opposition candidates.

"According to our analysis of the number of articles, excluding paid items, published in Croatian dailies and weeklies, the president and the HDZ were placed at the bottom, even in the so-called state media," Pasalic said.
The report cited one nine-day period in the campaign, timed to the second, when Tudjman's campaign coverage was 300 times greater than that of Social Democrat candidate Zdravko Tomac.
The opposition leaders, who had raised the same objections as the OSCE during the campaign and already branded it biased and undemocratic, endorsed the international body's report.
Ivica Racan, the head of the Social Democratic party (SDP), cited a fresh example to support his case.

"Today's report by Croatian radio which left out the bit about the elections being unfair and just reported that the OSCE found them free just goes to prove that the election has in fact not been fair," Racan said.
"This is just another example of the filtering of information continuing, but it can only work for a short time."
He said the OSCE report supported their previous assessment that the level of democracy in Sunday's election was lower in comparison to past elections.
"The presenting of candidates in the media has not been equal...and at the same time there was a big smear campaign being waged against the other two presidential candidates," Racan said.

The SDP will attempt to get data from parliament on the HDZ's financing of the elections, "as the banquet and the fireworks alone have cost more than the whole SDP campaign", he said referring to Tudjman's lavish election-night party.
